newsitem.title: USA: Emerging debt ends mixed as bids find no follow-up.
newsitem.headline: Emerging debt ends mixed as bids find no follow-up.

text.p: Emerging market debt prices found little support for an intense U.S. Treasury-driven surge and finished Friday narrowly mixed, traders said.
"It was dealer-driven," said one brady bond trader at a U.S. investment bank. "There were probably a few dealers scrambling around after being caught short."
Brady traders saw the moves as a technical rebound. Players got caught up in a bidding frenzy but found little sustained interest to keep up prices.
"There was no interest. It was a typical Friday afternoon," said one Brady dealer at a U.S. bank.
Argentine FRBs ARFLC05=RR finished up 1/8 to 82-3/8, while Brazilian C bonds BR8D14=RR slipped 1/8 to 71-5/8 amd Mexico's global bond due 2026 MXUMS=RR closed unchanged at 99-3/4.
Traders said they saw little evidence of portfolio flows coming into the market, which was likely to remain strong, barring any major shocks.
"What you've got is the market being pulled back and forth by proprietary books," said one emerging market portfolio manager. "They are just throwing paper back and forth at each other."
